Files app engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume FileProvider integration covers storefront language. Xcode, entitlements, and App Store Connect actually separate file-manager behavior from product-page copy:

  • FileProvider extensions & document providers — in-app code that exposes custom file locations under Files → Browse. Controls which folders buyers see. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • Files → Browse locations sidebar — Recents, Shared, On My iPhone, iCloud Drive, Downloads, Tags, and third-party providers. Your listing may show this hub on screenshots; teaching buyers where files live is listing copy, not engineering work.
  • Connect to Server (SMB / WebDAV / FTP) — buyer-facing network file access from the Files app. Product-page claims about remote servers are listing scope — not something AppLocale configures on buyer devices.
  • Folder management & Tags — create, rename, move, compress, and tag files inside 文件. Description and caption fields explain value; implementing storage behavior is outside AppLocale.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of FileProvider being enabled.

A buyer who uses the Files app and a localized China listing are both important when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Files app–specific listing copy — what translates differently

File-manager listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe Apple's Files app — not a literal paste of US marketing:

文件 and Browse hub phrasing

US pages use "Files", "Browse", "All your files in one place", or "Manage documents on iPhone." Apple's consumer-facing Simplified Chinese vocabulary uses 文件 for the app, 浏览 for the Browse tab, 最近项目 for Recents, 共享 for Shared, 本机 or 我的 iPhone for On My iPhone, 下载项 for Downloads, and 标签 for Tags. AppLocale aligns phrasing with Apple's storefront terms while keeping your app's voice — not inventing file-management capabilities your app does not support.

Browse locations sidebar

Screenshots that show the Files app with multiple browse locations — Recents at top, Shared below, On My iPhone and iCloud Drive as peer locations, Downloads and Tags in the sidebar — need captions that name the hub, not generic "cloud storage" copy meant for the iCloud Drive guide. A frame showing the full Browse tree is Files app listing scope when the file manager is the hero.

Connect to Server and remote folders

Some listings reference SMB, WebDAV, or FTP access through Files → Connect to Server — "Access network drives from iPhone" blurbs. These are factual product claims in description or screenshot copy when your English listing makes them — 连接服务器, 连接服务器以浏览文件 — not substitutes for implementing network protocols in your app, which AppLocale does not engineer.

Document provider extensions

Marketing may mention third-party locations appearing under Browse — cloud services, NAS apps, or enterprise file providers. zh-Hans copy should describe buyer-visible benefits concisely — 浏览第三方文件位置, 文档提供程序 — without over-claiming provider integrations your English listing does not state.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need file-manager search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 文件, 文件管理, 浏览, and 最近项目 each signal different intent from generic productivity or iCloud sync keywords.

Official-style zh-Hans glossary — Files app Browse hub

Use Apple's consumer-facing Simplified Chinese terms on listing frames that mirror system UI — not invented translations:

  • Files app → 文件
  • Browse (tab) → 浏览
  • Recents → 最近项目
  • Shared → 共享
  • On My iPhone / On My iPad → 本机 / 我的 iPhone / 我的 iPad
  • iCloud Drive (location) → iCloud 云盘 — one browse location, not the hero on this page
  • Downloads → 下载项
  • Tags → 标签
  • Connect to Server → 连接服务器
  • New Folder → 新建文件夹
  • Compress → 压缩
  • Document Provider / third-party location → 文档提供程序 / 第三方位置

When a screenshot shows only one location — for example iCloud Drive folders without the Browse hub — use the iCloud Drive listing guide. When the frame is a document picker sheet from your app, use the document browser guide.
